2018_123_071718regmtg.paragraph: Agenda and supporting packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of July 17, 2018 at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Business includes a consent agenda of June 5, June 12 and June 19, 2018 minutes plus Michigan High School Athletic Association membership for August 1, 2018 through July 31, 2019; the appointments of Christine Foren as Supervisor and Jessica Carrier as Director of Special Education; and a contract extension for Superintendent Richard Machesky through June 30, 2021. The central action is certifying ballot language for a replacement operating millage of 21 mills, with 18 mills the maximum allowable levy, for the November 6, 2018 election, estimated to yield $22,644,260 during the 2018 calendar year.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 PM, July 17, 2018, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Item 5 — General Consent Agenda**
Minutes of the June 5, 2018 Board meeting; the June 12, 2018 special meeting and closed session; the June 12, 2018 workshop; the June 19, 2018 Board meeting; and a Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) membership resolution enrolling the district's six secondary schools from August 1, 2018 through July 31, 2019.

**Item 6 — Personnel**

| Action | Person | Terms |
|---|---|---|
| Supervisor, Special Education | Christine Foren | Two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective July 1, 2018 |
| Director, Special Education | Jessica Carrier | Two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective July 1, 2018 |
| Superintendent contract extension | Dr. Richard Machesky | July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2021, without tenure |
| Cabinet extensions | Mark Dziatczak, Rick West, Kris Griffor, Jordan Harris | Successor contracts commencing July 1, 2018 and terminating June 30, 2020 |
| Administrative personnel extensions | Named principals, assistant principals, an associate principal and directors | Through June 30, 2020, or as otherwise indicated in the individual contract, subject to the Administrative Handbook layoff provision |

The Special Education Supervisor search drew 86 applications; four external applicants (Jill Gregg, Jennifer Egan, Maureen Schabel, Camilla Giberson) were interviewed, and a second round comprised one external candidate plus four internal candidates (Karly Didocha, Christine Foren, Camilla Giberson, Chris Olson, Tonya Romancheck). Final selection: Christine Foren.

**Item 7 — Curriculum**
MHSAA has approved adding Troy High School to the Boys' and Girls' Skiing cooperative team with Athens High School, Avondale High School and Berkley High School for the 2018-19 and 2019-20 school years.

**Item 8 — Business: Replacement Operating Millage**
Resolution certifying ballot wording to the Clerk of the County of Oakland, the School District Election Coordinator, by no later than August 14, 2018 under Act 116, Public Acts of Michigan, 1954, for the General School Election of November 6, 2018.

| Ballot element | Figure |
|---|---|
| Limitation increase requested | 21 mills |
| Maximum allowable levy | 18 mills ($18.00 per $1,000 of taxable valuation) |
| Replacement portion | 17.684 mills |
| Restoration portion | 0.316 mills |
| Term | Eight (8) years, 2018 to 2025 inclusive |
| Protection against future Headlee rollbacks | Up to 3 mills |
| Estimated revenue, 2018 calendar year | $22,644,260 |

The existing authority, approved by voters in 2015, expires with the district's 2025 tax levy on December 31, 2025. The levy applies to non-homestead property, principally industrial and commercial real property and residential rental property; owner-occupied homes and qualified agricultural property are exempt.

**Attached minutes highlights**
The June 5 meeting at Athens High School was Youth Recognition Night, with roughly 300 in the audience and dozens of academic, athletic and arts awards read into the record. The June 19 meeting at the Services Building opened with a public hearing on the 2018-2019 proposed budget presented by Rick West and approved materials purchases of $1,023,927.97 (grades 6-12 social studies) and $665,874.91 (elementary science), a $43,483.92 musical string instruments bid to Shar Music & Products Company, and a $284,350.00 Boulan Park Middle School old office bid pack.

Board meeting agenda and complete supporting packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of July 17, 2018, convening at 7:00 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000. The cover page notes that when school is in session Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and may also be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda sequence is Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions and Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Adjournment.

**Item 5 — General Consent Agenda.** Items A through E are: minutes of the June 5, 2018 Board of Education meeting; minutes of the June 12, 2018 Special Board of Education Meeting and Closed Session; minutes of the June 12, 2018 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the June 19, 2018 Board of Education meeting; and a Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Membership Resolution for 2018/2019. The MHSAA resolution enrolls the six (6) secondary schools under the direction of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, City of Troy, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc., a voluntary nonprofit corporation, and enrolls them to participate in approved interschool athletic activities. It delegates supervision and control to the Superintendent or designee, accepts the association's Constitution and By-Laws and the rules, regulations and interpretations published in the current HANDBOOK as minimum standards, and is effective from August 1, 2018 until July 31, 2019, during which period the authorization may not be revoked.

**June 5, 2018 minutes (Athens High School).** President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present in addition to Mr. Schmidt were Board members Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart, along with Superintendent Machesky; administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris, Jolly and West; and approximately 300 members of the audience. The evening was Youth Recognition Night. Mike Jolly and the Board recognized the girls' synchronized swim team for winning the state championship, All-State athletes in winter sports, and senior scholar athletes from winter and spring sports who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program. Board members then read an extensive list of student academic awards spanning the AMC8 American Mathematics Contest (two Boulan Park students placed 1st and 2nd nationally), the American Scholastic Achievement League, the 13th Annual Chinese Bridge Speech Contest held March 31 at the University of Massachusetts in Boston, the 2018 Chinese Zodiac Art Contest held February 27 at Schoolcraft College in Livonia, CLASS Gold and Silver Apple Awards, the 50th Michigan Student Film Festival at the Detroit Institute of Arts' Detroit Film Theatre on April 28 (a Larson student won Best in Show for a documentary on the Bosnian War), DECA International Competition in Atlanta, the FIRST Robotics World Competition (the International Academy-East team took 30th place in the Curie Division), the Larson Robo Rebels #12549 First Tech Challenge team, Future Problem Solving, Generation Nano, HOSA, the Intel Science and Engineering Fair (where "Context-Aware Medical Image Super-Resolution using Convolutional Neural Networks" was awarded second place by the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence), the Michigan Japanese Quiz Bowl at Eastern Michigan University, MATHCOUNTS (Boulan Park placed 1st in State, 7th and 12th in Nation), the Michigan Brain Bee, the Michigan China Quiz Bowl, the Michigan Council for Economic Education, Michigan History Day (a Boulan Park group website titled "The Internment of Japanese Americans"), MITES, MIPA journalism awards, the Michigan Japanese Speech Contest, the Michigan Junior Chess Championship, the Michigan Mathematics League, MSBOA and MSVMA music events, the NATAS Michigan Student Production Awards, the National Economics Challenge, the National French Contest, the National Geographic Bee, the National German Exam, the National High School Biology Scholarship (the Athens team won 1st place in the U.S.), the National History Bee, the National Spanish Exam, the National Spelling Bee, the National Youth Arts Awards (the Troy Theatre Ensemble earned 3 awards and 11 additional nominations for the 2016-17 season), the President's Volunteer Service Award, the Purple Comet Math Contest (Boulan Park tied for 1st in State as a team with Detroit Country Day School under the team name "Pulverizing Pancake"), Quiz Bowl, Scholastic Art and Writing Gold Key Awards, the Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit at Cobo Hall, the Science Olympiad State Competition (Troy High placed 1st in State in Anatomy and Physiology, Materials Science, Microbe Mission and Optics), the Siemens Foundation Math and Science Research Competition, the Sutton Foster Ovation Musical Theater Awards at Michigan State University, the U.S. Senate Youth Program with its $10,000 college scholarship, Model United Nations conferences at the University of Chicago and the University of Toronto, the 24th Annual University of Toronto National Biology Competition held April 26 with 4,809 eligible contestants from 362 schools, the USA Biology Olympiad, the Washington University Chemistry Tournament (Troy High's first team entry, against 54 other teams), and the WordMasters Challenge. Additions and Deletions and Public Communication on agenda items were both None. Resolution 18-053, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved consent items A, B and C — minutes of the May 1, 2018 workshop, minutes of the May 15, 2018 meeting, and a Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2018/2019 School Year Budget — Yes 7, No 0. Student representatives Hana Barre (Troy High), Nadia Shaouni (Troy College & Career High School), and Tori Zarbaugh (Athens High School) gave end-of-year updates; Anjana Pisupati (International Academy-East) was not in attendance. Mr. Miletti announced the TFEE Anthony Spagnola Golf Outing on June 22 at Sanctuary Lake Golf Course. Dr. Machesky announced that all school buildings will display four bright world class pillars symbolizing the strategic plan: prioritizing learning, empowering students, attending to the social, emotional and physical well-being of all, and investing in early childhood. Mr. Schmidt announced a Board Workshop on June 12 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building and a regular meeting on June 19 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building. The meeting was adjourned at 8:42 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

**June 12, 2018 special meeting and closed session.** President Schmidt called the special meeting to order at 5:02 p.m. at the Administration Building with Board members Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart and Superintendent Machesky present; there were no members of the audience. Resolution 18-062, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Dr. Philippart, provided that as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Board go into closed session to discuss Superintendent Evaluation. The roll call recorded Yes votes from Philippart, Schmidt, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Miletti. The Board moved to Closed Session at 5:03 p.m. and the meeting reconvened at 5:05 p.m.; the special meeting adjourned at 6:27 p.m. Separate closed session minutes record the closed session called to order at 5:05 p.m. with the same members and the Superintendent present, no one else present during the discussion on Superintendent Evaluation, no other business conducted, and adjournment at 6:28 p.m.

**June 12, 2018 Board Workshop.** Called to order at 6:30 p.m. at the Administration Building with all seven Board members, Superintendent Machesky, administrators Dziatczak, Griffor, Gottlieb, Harris and West, Curriculum & Instruction Specialist Julia Alder and a history teacher present, plus one member of the audience. The agenda covered Public Communication; a Teaching & Learning update on Secondary Social Studies Materials Adoption and Elementary Science Materials Adoption; a Business Services update on the Musical String Instruments Bid, the Old Office at Boulan Park Middle School, Food Service Contract Renewal, and the 2017/2018 Final Budget Amendment and Proposed 2018/2019 Budget; an Employee Services staffing update; and Board Professional Learning on Recess. The meeting adjourned at 9:57 p.m.

**June 19, 2018 Board meeting (Services Building).** President Schmidt began at 7:01 p.m. with a public hearing on the 2018-2019 proposed budget. Mr. West presented the proposed budget with a PowerPoint, noting it had been reviewed in detail at the June 12 workshop, and addressed tax values, homestead and non-homestead millages, general fund assumptions, the foundation allowance, increased student enrollment, revenues and expenditures. With no questions from Board members or the audience, the public hearing closed at 7:20 p.m. Present were all seven Board members, Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris, Gottlieb, Cross, Morse and West, and approximately 100 additional members of the audience. The Mission Moment recognized the Baker Middle School Shark Tank project, guided by teachers Anne Costello, Lisa Gaglio and Lori Ulewicz, with 8th graders Mina Tobya, Julianne Pabalan, Mary Sankarathil, Lydia Burns and Vivan O presenting their project "Paramount Style." During public communication, Shruthi Sunilkumar of 723 Palermo in Troy, a Troy High student, described a "Kite Festival" fundraiser planned for July 8 from 1 to 5 p.m. at Boulan Park and her nonprofit Kids 2 Kids, which provides bicycles and helmets for foster children. Resolution 18-054, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved consent items A through E: the Treasurer's Report for April and May 2018; the 2017/2018 Budget Amendment; the 2018/2019 Budget Appropriations Resolution; the Food Service Contract Renewal; and an MDE Update on Significant Disproportionality Finding of Black Students in the 2015-2016 School Year (Yes 7, No 0). Personnel resolutions each passed Yes 7, No 0 and each issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective July 1, 2018: 18-055, moved by Mrs. Hammond and supported by Mr. Gottlieb, appointed Ms. Michelle Barsh Principal of Martell Elementary School; 18-056, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Hauff, appointed Ms. Cassandra Conaton Assistant Principal of Baker Middle School; 18-057, moved by Mr. Gottlieb and supported by Dr. Philippart, appointed Ms. Kristy Pierce Assistant Principal of Boulan Park Middle School. Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak and Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, reported on curriculum materials. Resolution 18-058, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Dr. Philippart, approved recommended social studies materials for grades 6-12 in the amount of $1,023,927.97 for the 2018-2019 school year (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 18-059, moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved recommended elementary science materials in the amount of $665,874.91 for 2018-2019 (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 18-060, moved by Mrs. Hammond and supported by Mr. Gottlieb, awarded the musical string instruments bid to Shar Music & Products Company in the amount of $43,483.92 as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 18-061, moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Hauff, awarded bid pack 24 for the Old Office at Boulan Park Middle School and approved $284,350.00 as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, allocated as DKI, Inc. demolition $8,900.00; Construction Solutions, Inc. general trades $145,800.00; Contrast Mechanical mechanical $48,700.00; MCMI, Inc temperature controls $12,500.00; Shoreview Electrical, Inc. electrical $42,600; and contingency $25,850.00, for a total of $284,350.00 (Yes 7, No 0). Superintendent Machesky shared a "2017-2018 School Year in Review" video assembled by Kerry Birmingham. Mrs. Fleming congratulated Cable Supervisor Karen Rockwell on her retirement. Mr. Schmidt announced the next regular meeting at the Administration Building on July 17 at 7:00 p.m. The meeting adjourned at 8:42 p.m.

**Item 6.A — Supervisor, Special Education.** Recommendation to appoint Ms. Christine Foren, who began her education career as a Special Education teacher for Fraser Public Schools in 2006 and joined the Troy School District as a Special Education teacher at Troy High School in 2017. She holds a Bachelor's Degree in Psychology and Special Education from Grand Valley State University and an Endorsement in Secondary Administration from Saginaw Valley State University, and is pursuing a Special Education Supervisor Certificate from Saginaw Valley State University. Her attached resume gives an address of 2700 Warwick Drive, Bloomfield Hills, MI 48304, phone (586) 601-9458, and lists her Grand Valley State University B.S. from 2000-2006 with endorsements in Emotionally and Cognitively Impaired (K-12) and General Education (K-5), Saginaw Valley State University Educational Leadership: Principalship from 2009-2011, Teacher Consultant service from 2012-2016, Acting Administrator roles at Fraser Public Schools from 2011-2017, a 2011 administrative internship at Richards Middle School involving 100+ hours of shadowing, Richards Middle School Special Education Department Chair from 2010-2017, School Improvement Team Co-Chair from 2011-2017, the Galileo Leader Consortium at Oakland Schools from 2013-2015, Macomb Intermediate School District Teacher Leader Cohort IV from 2011-2013, head coach of 7th grade girls basketball from 2007-2013, a State of Michigan School Administrator Certificate held since 2011 and a Professional Teaching Certificate since 2006. References listed are Steven Berg of the Macomb Intermediate School District, (586) 228-3454; Jessica Carrier, Troy School District, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; Huston Julian, Richards Middle School Principal, Fraser Public Schools, 33500 Garfield, Fraser, MI 48026, (586) 439-7495; Dr. Richard Repicky, 9572 Mandon, White Lake, MI 48386, (248) 366-4975; and Remo Roncone, Troy High School Principal, 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098, (248) 823-2720. The search summary records that 86 applications were submitted, that four external applicants were granted interviews — Jill Gregg, Jennifer Egan, Maureen Schabel and Camilla Giberson — and that the second round included one external candidate plus four internal candidates: Karly Didocha, Christine Foren, Camilla Giberson, Chris Olson and Tonya Romancheck, with Christine Foren the final selection.

**Item 6.B — Director, Special Education.** Recommendation to appoint Ms. Jessica Carrier, who began her education career with Fraser Public Schools as a Special Education Teacher in 1999, served as Assistant Technical Consultant for Special Education from 2000 to 2004, became Special Education Consultant in 2003, Middle School Assistant Principal in 2004, Middle School Principal in 2011 and Director of Special Education in 2015, then accepted the position of Supervisor of Special Education for the Troy School District in 2017. She holds a Bachelor of Arts in Special Education from Central Michigan University and a Master's in Educational Administration and Specialist Degree in Educational Leadership from Saginaw Valley State University. The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective July 1, 2018.

**Item 6.C — Superintendent's contract extension.** The Board recently completed Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation, reporting that he completed his fourth year as a highly effective superintendent and exceeded expectations in all evaluation categories, and citing his support of oneTROY and the "World Class by 2020 Vision" shared at the start of the 2017-18 school year with its four pillars: Prioritize Learning, Empower Students, Attend to Well-Being, and Invest in Early Childhood. The resolution extends his contract from July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2021, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to the written Agreement.

**Item 6.D — Cabinet contract extensions.** The Superintendent recommends contract extensions for Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; and Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services. Their current contracts expire on June 30, 2019; the successor contracts commence July 1, 2018 and terminate June 30, 2020, without tenure in the administrative positions.

**Item 6.E — Extension of administrative personnel contracts.** Contracts are extended through June 30, 2020, or as otherwise indicated in the individual contract, without tenure and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook, for Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal, International Academy-East; Lara Dixon, Principal, Athens High School; Remo Roncone, Principal, Troy High School; Joe Duda, Principal, Larson Middle School; Joyce Brasington, Principal, Wattles Elementary School; Brian Canfield, Principal, Schroeder Elementary School; Mike Cottone, Principal, Troy Union Elementary School; Erin Detmer, Principal, Leonard Elementary School; Tammy DiPonio, Principal, Costello Elementary School; Sarah Glasser, Principal, Hamilton Elementary School; Matt Jansen, Principal, Wass Elementary School; Melanie Morey, Principal, Barnard Elementary School; Jeremey Whan, Principal, Bemis Elementary School; Stephanie Zendler, Principal, Morse Elementary School; Melissa Curth, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Robert Dowd, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Dan House, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Dan Mills, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; William Turner, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Brian Zawislak, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Amy Buchanan, Assistant Principal, Smith Middle School; David Recker, Assistant Principal, Larson Middle School; Kerry Birmingham, Director, Communications & Strategic Initiatives; Rob Carson, Director, Maintenance and Operations; Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity & Accountability; Christin Silagy, Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments; and Elizabeth Soggs, Director, Technology.

**Item 7.A — High School Cooperative Team Agreement.** The district received MHSAA approval to add Troy High School to the cooperative team in Boys' and Girls' Skiing with Athens High School, Avondale High School and Berkley High School. The resolution commits Troy High School to join those schools to fund, support and maintain the cooperative skiing team for the 2018-19 and 2019-20 school years, with a copy of the resolution to accompany the renewal agreement form sent to the MHSAA.

**Item 8.A — Resolution to submit replacement operating millage proposal.** The Board determined it necessary for continuing operation to restore and replace the authority to levy 18 mills for operating purposes on non-homestead property, previously approved by voters in 2015 and rolled back by application of the Headlee Amendment to the Michigan Constitution, and to increase the prior authority in the event of future rollbacks. The proposal is to be submitted at the General School Election of November 6, 2018, and the ballot wording must be certified to the Clerk of the County of Oakland, State of Michigan — the School District Election Coordinator — not later than August 14, 2018, as required by Act 116, Public Acts of Michigan, 1954, as amended. The resolution directs the Election Coordinator to post and publish notice of the last day of registration and notice of election and to have ballots prepared and printed in the form of Exhibit A, and rescinds conflicting resolutions. It is signed by Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education, with a certification that the resolution was adopted at a regular meeting held July 17, 2018 in compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Exhibit A, the Replacement Operating Millage Proposal for the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, explains that the proposal would restore and replace the authority to levy the statutory limit of 18 mills on non-homestead property (principally industrial and commercial real property and residential rental property), which currently expires with the district's 2025 tax levy, and allow continued levy of the statutory limit of 18 mills in the event of future Headlee rollbacks of up to 3 mills, allowing the district to continue receiving revenues at the full per pupil foundation allowance permitted by the State. Owner occupied homes and qualified agricultural property are exempt. The ballot question asks whether the limitation on total taxes assessed against all property except principal residences and other property exempted by law within the Troy School District be increased in the amount of 21 mills, with 18 mills being the maximum allowable levy ($18.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation), for a period of eight (8) years, 2018 to 2025 inclusive, with 17.684 mills of the 21 mills being a replacement of authorized millage that would otherwise expire on December 31, 2025 and 0.316 mills being a restoration of millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution. The proposal states that the operating millage, if approved and levied, would provide estimated revenues to the School District of $22,644,260 during the 2018 calendar year, to be used for general operating purposes.
